prerequisites_stated_in_text: Advanced Modules 1--16. Risk management is treated strictly inside the execution of ICT models. Generic trading-psychology content is omitted; only the disciplines that protect narrative-driven process are included.

Recognise and stop overtrading and revenge trading the moment they appear.
Retire models and bias immediately upon narrative invalidation.
Maintain the psychological discipline required to stand aside when no model is authorised.

concepts.name: Invalidation as the Core Risk Concept
concepts.definition:
Stops are placed at levels that, if reached, negate the premise of the trade:
- Beyond the far side of the entry PD array,
- Beyond the origin of the displacement that created the array,
- Beyond a structural point whose breach would invalidate the internal or external MSS.
- Arbitrary fixed-pip or fixed-percentage stops that ignore the narrative geometry are inferior. A stop that is "too wide" relative to the first target may simply mean the trade is not worth taking; it does not justify moving the stop closer to a non-logical level.

raw_sections.Trade vs Narrative Invalidation:
As established in Module 16: trade invalidation ends the specific entry; narrative invalidation ends the bias and forbids further models in the old direction. Both are defined before entry and are respected without negotiation.

**Evidence Classification:** *A/B - Logical, structure- and array-based invalidation is consistent with ICT practice; fixed-pip stops are not ICT doctrine.*

concepts.name: Position Sizing
concepts.definition: Position size is calculated from the distance between entry and trade invalidation so that the monetary (or percentage) loss at the stop equals a predetermined risk unit (commonly 0.25 - 1 % of equity, chosen by the individual and held constant). Formula conceptually: Size = (Account risk amount) / (Entry - Invalidation distance).

concepts.name: Maximum Daily Risk and Daily Loss Limit
concepts.definition: A hard ceiling on the sum of risk committed across all trades in a session (e.g., 1 - 2 % of equity). When the ceiling is reached, no new risk is added even if a perfect model appears.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: A hard ceiling on the sum of risk committed across all trades in a session (e.g., 1 - 2 % of equity). When the ceiling is reached, no new risk is added even if a perfect model appears.
detection_criteria: unspecified - see raw_sections

raw_sections.Maximum Daily Risk: A hard ceiling on the sum of risk committed across all trades in a session (e.g., 1 - 2 % of equity). When the ceiling is reached, no new risk is added even if a perfect model appears.
raw_sections.Daily Loss Limit: A hard floor on realised plus unrealised loss for the day (e.g., 1 - 3 % of equity). When the limit is hit, trading for that session terminates. The purpose is to protect the account from the sequence of decisions that often follows early losses.
raw_sections.Relationship to Narrative: Daily limits are process controls. They do not improve the quality of any single ICT model; they prevent the destruction of capital when the day's narrative is difficult or the trader's execution is impaired.

concepts.name: Risk/Reward as Outcome, Not Filter
concepts.definition:
In ICT narrative trading, the geometry of the delivery leg (entry at a discount/premium array, target at a liquidity pool) produces a risk/reward ratio as a consequence. That ratio is observed and recorded; it is not used as a primary filter that rejects an otherwise perfect narrative-aligned model solely because the ratio is "only" 1.5 : 1 or 2 : 1. Conversely, a high R:R that requires a non-logical stop or a fantasy target is not a justification for taking a low-quality narrative. Narrative quality first; R:R is the measured result.

**Evidence Classification:** *C - The explicit ranking of narrative quality above a fixed R:R threshold is advanced process synthesis consistent with ICT's emphasis on delivery and liquidity over mechanical filters.*

concepts.name: Partial Profit-Taking and Target Liquidity
concepts.definition: Partial exits at the first high-quality intermediate pool (Module 3 liquidity hierarchy) reduce risk and lock a portion of the narrative's expected delivery. The remaining runner continues toward the terminal Draw on Liquidity while the narrative remains valid.

concepts.name: Model Invalidation
concepts.definition:
When the narrative or bias is invalidated:
- Open positions that depended on the old narrative are closed or managed to the new invalidation.
- No new entries in the old direction are permitted.
- A new narrative and bias must be constructed before any opposing model is authorised.
- Model invalidation is not optional. Continuing to trade a retired model is a process failure.

concepts.name: Overtrading
concepts.definition: Overtrading is the taking of trades that fail the model-selection filters of Module 15 or the pre-entry checklist of Module 16, usually because the student feels the need to be in the market. It includes: trading outside the authorised session window, trading when bias is unclear, trading lower-quality arrays, and adding risk after the daily risk ceiling has been reached.

concepts.name: Revenge Trading
concepts.definition: Revenge trading is the attempt to recover a loss by immediately taking another trade that would not have been authorised by the narrative and filters. It is almost always accompanied by increased size, loosened invalidation, or both.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Revenge trading is the attempt to recover a loss by immediately taking another trade that would not have been authorised by the narrative and filters. It is almost always accompanied by increased size, loosened invalidation, or both.

raw_sections.Definition: Revenge trading is the attempt to recover a loss by immediately taking another trade that would not have been authorised by the narrative and filters. It is almost always accompanied by increased size, loosened invalidation, or both.
raw_sections.Counter-Measure: After a losing trade, the student returns to the narrative stack and the selection procedure. If the narrative is still valid and a new qualifying sequence appears, a normal-sized trade may be taken. If the narrative is invalidated or no sequence appears, the session continues with no further risk. The daily loss limit is the final backstop.

concepts.name: Psychological Discipline Specific to ICT Process
concepts.definition:
The disciplines required by this textbook are narrow and concrete:
- Stand aside when bias is unclear or no model is authorised.
- Wait for the full LTF conditioning sequence; do not anticipate.
- Respect both trade and narrative invalidation without moving stops farther away.
- Accept "no trade today" as a successful process outcome.
- Do not increase size to recover losses.
- Do not trade a model that the selection filters have rejected.
- These are process rules, not personality goals. They are either followed or they are not; the equity curve records the difference.

worked_narrative_examples.name: Worked Risk Example
worked_narrative_examples.definition:
Account equity: 100 000. Risk per trade: 0.5 % = 500. Daily loss limit: 1.5 % = 1 500. Daily risk ceiling: 1.5 %.

Selected model: long at 1.0650, trade invalidation 1.0620 (30 pips). Position size is set so that 30 pips = 500 risk.

First target: 1.0780 (partial 50 %). Terminal: 1.1200 (runner).

If stopped: loss 500; remaining daily risk capacity 1 000; narrative still intact, so a second qualifying trade remains possible.

If daily loss limit is later reached: trading stops for the session even if a third perfect model appears.

If weekly invalidation prints while the runner is open: runner is closed; bias is rewritten; no further longs until a new bullish narrative is constructed.

evidence_summary.name: Evidence Summary
evidence_summary.definition:
Logical, structure- and liquidity-based invalidation, targeting of liquidity pools, and the subordination of risk parameters to narrative quality are consistent with ICT emphasis on delivery and institutional order flow. Specific percentage risk limits, daily loss limits, and the formal ranking of narrative above fixed R:R thresholds are advanced process controls that protect the application of ICT models; they are not themselves ICT price-action doctrine.

***Source / Research note:** Primary orientation: ICT practice of array- and structure-based stops and liquidity targets. Position-sizing formulas, daily limits, and anti-revenge rules are standard professional risk process applied to the ICT narrative framework.*

no_trade_conditions.statement: Overtrading = taking trades that fail the model-selection filters (Module 15) or the pre-entry checklist (Module 16), usually from feeling the need to be in the market -- includes trading outside the authorised session window, trading when bias is unclear, trading lower-quality arrays, and adding risk after the daily risk ceiling has been reached. Revenge trading = attempting to recover a loss by immediately taking another trade not authorised by the narrative and filters, almost always accompanied by increased size or loosened invalidation -- after a loss, return to the narrative stack and selection procedure; if invalidated or no sequence appears, take no further risk (daily loss limit is the final backstop). Do not use fixed-pip stops that ignore the array and structure. Do not reject a high-quality narrative solely because R:R is below an arbitrary number. Do not widen the stop after entry 'to give it room.' Do not continue trading after the daily loss limit has been hit. Do not revenge-size the next trade after a loss. Do not treat 'I need to make back the loss' as a valid reason to select a model. Do not ignore narrative invalidation because the trade is still open and 'might come back.'

When the narrative or bias is invalidated: open positions that depended on the old narrative are closed or managed to the new invalidation; no new entries in the old direction are permitted; a new narrative and bias must be constructed before any opposing model is authorised. Continuing to trade a retired model is a process failure.

key_terms: Logical stop - invalidation placed at array, displacement origin, or structural failure point.
Risk per trade - predetermined fraction of equity risked on a single idea.
Daily risk ceiling - maximum sum of risk committed in one session.
Daily loss limit - maximum realised + unrealised loss that terminates the session.
R:R as outcome - risk/reward measured from narrative geometry, not used as a primary filter.
Model invalidation - retirement of a model when its supporting narrative fails.
Overtrading - taking trades that fail the selection or pre-entry filters.
Revenge trading - attempting to recover a loss with an unauthorised or oversized trade.
